metadata.case_name: WONG SHUK LEI v. LEUNG MING KWONG

injuries.description: Soft tissue injury / lumbar spine involvement with tenderness at L4/5 and L5/S1 and decreased range of motion
source: tenderness elicited at the L4/5 and L5/S1 levels, maximal over her left paraspinal regions. The range of motion of her lumbar spine, in terms of flexion, extension, left and right lateral bending, had substantially decreased. She had reached a state of maximum medical improvement.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

source: she still suffers back pain, face injury (eye twitching), and psychological impacts.
the plaintiff was sitting at an aisle seat in a coach. The defendant negligently drove a car, which hit the coach. She was thrown forward with her left face hit against her front seat.
she still suffers back pain, face injury (eye twitching), and psychological impacts.

manifestations.description: Tenderness elicited at the L4/5 and L5/S1 levels, maximal over her left paraspinal regions
Substantially decreased range of motion of the lumbar spine (flexion, extension, left and right lateral bending)
Unable to stand long or sit low due to back pain

treatments_received: Accident and Emergency attendances at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (A & E QEH)
Admission from 30.5.04 to 1.6.04 for anxiety and fear (Psychological) at TKOH
Psychological treatment (multiple entries listed as Anxiety and fear at TKOH)
Consultation with orthopaedic specialist Dr. Li Wing Kin (report after consultation on 19 March 2005)

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Siu Lun v Hui Cho Yee & Anor
comparable_cases.injury_description: Fractured odontoid which has healed; Soft tissue injury at left side and low back; Mild pain or discomfort which might increase slightly as he got older; Mild depressive mood which was likely to dissipate upon conclusion of trial.
